title: NRP internal probe into Taser incident nearing end
article: With the Special Investigations Unit probe into the death of James Foldi completed, the Niagara Regional Police anticipate concluding its own internal investigation sometime "in the near future," says chief Wendy Southall.

"As required by the regulations to the Police Services Act, I have caused a parallel internal investigation to be conducted. That investigation will determine whether the incident raises any discipline issues and will review other Taser-related matters," said Southall in a statement released last Thursday. "Given that the Special Investigations Unit investigation is now completed, I expect our internal investigation will be concluded in the near future."

Last Thursday, the SIU released the results of their investigation into the incident, which was sparked by Foldi's death on July 1. Foldi died after being arrested following a series of break-ins to homes in the Crescent Avenue and Village Park Drive area in Beamsville. A Taser was used in an attempt to subdue Foldi during a struggle prior to his arrest.

In the SIU report, the Director of the SIU, James Cornish, said he found no reasonable grounds to believe that any NRP officers were criminally responsible for Foldi's death. The SIU did not release a cause of death, but said Foldi had a "potentially lethal amount of an illegal substance in his system at the time of his death." Foldi's brother, Steven, said in an interview last week, identified the illegal substance as cocaine.

After a brief chase, police discharged a Taser 12 times during a three-minute period while struggling with Foldi. At least one of those times it appears the Taser did not appear to touch Foldi, but the SIU is uncertain how many other times the Taser did make contact.

"It is unclear how many of those discharges made contact with Mr. Foldi. It must be remembered that the Taser was being used during the course of a violent struggle and thus it is likely that some of the discharges occurred while the Taser was not in contact with Mr. Foldi or if there was initial contact, that contact may have been broken by the movement of either the officer or Mr. Foldi. Mr. Foldi continued to struggle and breathe for some time after the Taser was used," said Cornish.

The SIU report says it was after Foldi was in custody that police noticed he was breathing heavily and called for an ambulance. Foldi lost consciousness and in spite of resuscitation efforts by both the police and paramedics and was pronounced dead in a hospital.
A post-mortem examination revealed no life-threatening injuries and no anatomical cause for Foldi's death.
In an interview with This Week prior to the SIU releasing its report, Steven Foldi said the family was not happy with the outcome.
"We're going to challenge it," Foldi said. "There's still a lot of unanswered questions people refuse to answer for us."
One of those questions, he said, surrounds the nature of his brother's death. Foldi says the family is puzzled.

"They're saying he overdosed, yet he left his home, apparently got in an altercation with a couple of people, and was able to run from the police," he said. "You don't run around the corner, have all the cops chasing you and get pepper sprayed and tased if you've ODed."
Foldi also said the family is considering civil action.
"Number one, we'd like some answers. Number two, we'd like the police to take some responsibility," he said, adding it is his understanding a public inquiry into the incident will be called.
